```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 4, fig.align = "center",
                      out.width = "100%")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Inputs. Set the working directory to wherever these live, or edit the paths.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

F_MACRO  <- "macro_k14_metrics.rds"
F_DEGEN  <- "degenerate_draw_test.rds"
F_CRIME  <- "experiement_crime_stage_8675309/crime_fcasts_k10.csv"
F_CRIMEA <- "experiement_crime_stage_8675309/crime_ablation_k10.csv"
F_MACROA <- "experiement_macro_stage_8675309/macro_ablation_k14.csv"

RUN_CRIME_SIG <- TRUE
F_CRIMEWS     <- "experiement_crime_stage_8675309/crime_k10_after_loop.RData"

has <- function(f) file.exists(f)

m <- if (has(F_MACRO)) readRDS(F_MACRO) else NULL
d <- if (has(F_DEGEN)) readRDS(F_DEGEN) else NULL

COL <- c(DGFC = "#1b4f72", BVAR = "#c0392b",
         DLM = "#7d8a2e", `SV-BVAR` = "#b7791f")

# Newey-West t on a loss differential. Positive => the DGFC is WORSE.
nw_t <- function(dd) {
  dd <- dd[is.finite(dd)]
  Tn <- length(dd)
  if (Tn < 10 || sd(dd) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  l <- floor(4 * (Tn / 100)^(2/9))
  g <- acf(dd, lag.max = l, type = "covariance", plot = FALSE)$acf
  v <- g[1] + 2 * sum((1 - seq_len(l) / (l + 1)) * g[-1])
  mean(dd) / sqrt(max(v, .Machine$double.eps) / Tn)
}
```


# Headline

```{r headline, results = "asis"}
if (is.null(m)) {
  cat("`", F_MACRO, "` not found.\n", sep = "")
} else {
  f  <- m$finals
  nn <- length(m$var_names)

  t_sv   <- sapply(1:nn, function(i) nw_t(m$dfc[, 4, i] - m$svbvar[, 4, i]))
  t_bvar <- sapply(1:nn, function(i) nw_t(m$dfc[, 4, i] - m$var[, 4, i]))
  t_dlm  <- sapply(1:nn, function(i) nw_t(m$dfc[, 4, i] - m$dlm[, 4, i]))

  cat(sprintf(
"The DGFC beats both competitors already in the paper, significantly, on every
series where a difference is detectable. It is statistically indistinguishable
from a modern stochastic-volatility BVAR on %d of %d macro series and
significantly behind on %d.

- vs the plain BVAR: DGFC significantly better on **%d of %d**
- vs the DLM: DGFC significantly better on **%d of %d**, never worse
- vs the SV BVAR: DGFC significantly worse on **%d of %d**, better on %d

Interval forecasting goes the other way. The DGFC has narrower 95%% intervals
than the SV BVAR on **%d of %d** series at mean coverage %.3f against the SV
BVAR's %.3f, so it is both sharper and closer to the 0.95 nominal. MSE is a tie
at %d to %d.

Significance throughout is a Newey-West t on the per-vintage CRPS differential,
significant at |t| > 1.96.
",
    sum(abs(t_sv) <= 1.96), nn, sum(t_sv > 1.96),
    sum(t_bvar < -1.96), nn,
    sum(t_dlm  < -1.96), nn,
    sum(t_sv   >  1.96), nn, sum(t_sv < -1.96),
    sum(f$dfc[, 3] < f$svbvar[, 3]), nn,
    mean(f$dfc[, 2]), mean(f$svbvar[, 2]),
    sum(f$dfc[, 1] < f$svbvar[, 1]), sum(f$svbvar[, 1] < f$dfc[, 1])))
}
```

# Macro, Table 2 at saturated k

```{r macro-write}
if (!is.null(m)) {
  f <- m$finals
  models <- c("DGFC", "BVAR", "DLM", "SV-BVAR")
  macro_lab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(m$var_names), function(i)
    data.frame(series = m$var_names[i], model = models,
               MSE  = round(c(f$dfc[i,1], f$var[i,1], f$dlm[i,1], f$svbvar[i,1]), 3),
               COV  = round(c(f$dfc[i,2], f$var[i,2], f$dlm[i,2], f$svbvar[i,2]), 3),
               SIZE = round(c(f$dfc[i,3], f$var[i,3], f$dlm[i,3], f$svbvar[i,3]), 3),
               CRPS = round(c(f$dfc[i,4], f$var[i,4], f$dlm[i,4], f$svbvar[i,4]), 3),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
  write.csv(macro_lab, "macro_table_k14_labeled.csv", row.names = FALSE)
}
```

The full four-metric table is in `macro_table_k14_labeled.csv`. Split here into
the two views that matter.

## Sharpness against calibration

Maximize sharpness subject to calibration, so the useful view is both at once.
Width is normalized by the DGFC's width for that series, since the fourteen
series differ in scale by three orders of magnitude.

```{r gneiting-plot, fig.height = 4.6}
if (!is.null(m)) {
  f  <- m$finals
  sz <- cbind(f$dfc[,3], f$var[,3], f$dlm[,3], f$svbvar[,3])
  cv <- cbind(f$dfc[,2], f$var[,2], f$dlm[,2], f$svbvar[,2])
  szn <- sz / sz[, 1]

  par(mar = c(4.2, 4.2, 2.2, 7.5), xpd = NA)
  plot(NA, xlim = range(szn) * c(0.8, 1.25), ylim = c(0.86, 1.01), log = "x",
       xlab = "interval width, relative to DGFC (log scale)",
       ylab = "empirical coverage", cex.lab = 0.9, cex.axis = 0.85,
       main = "Sharper is left, calibrated is the dashed line", cex.main = 1)
  par(xpd = FALSE)
  abline(h = 0.95, lty = 2)
  abline(v = 1, col = "grey85")
  for (j in 1:4) points(szn[, j], cv[, j], pch = 19, col = COL[j], cex = 1)
  legend(par("usr")[2] * 1.15, 1.0, names(COL), pch = 19, col = COL,
         bty = "o", cex = 0.85, xjust = -1, yjust = 2.5)
  par(xpd = FALSE)
}
```

The plain BVAR sits at coverage 1.000 on every series with intervals several
times wider, which is uninformative rather than good. The DLM over-covers at a
smaller width penalty. The SV BVAR is close to the DGFC on width and slightly
over-covers.

# Significance

\newpage

```{r sig-table}
if (!is.null(m)) {
  nn <- length(m$var_names)
  sig <- data.frame(
    series = m$var_names,
    pct_sv = round(100 * (m$finals$svbvar[,4] / m$finals$dfc[,4] - 1), 1),
    t_sv   = round(sapply(1:nn, function(i) nw_t(m$dfc[,4,i] - m$svbvar[,4,i])), 2),
    t_bvar = round(sapply(1:nn, function(i) nw_t(m$dfc[,4,i] - m$var[,4,i])), 2),
    t_dlm  = round(sapply(1:nn, function(i) nw_t(m$dfc[,4,i] - m$dlm[,4,i])), 2),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  sig <- sig[order(sig$t_sv, decreasing = TRUE), ]
  rownames(sig) <- NULL
  knitr::kable(sig, caption = "Positive t means the DGFC is worse. Significant at 5% beyond 1.96; Bonferroni across 14 tests is 2.91.")
}
```

```{r sig-plot, fig.height = 5}
if (!is.null(m)) {
  nn <- length(m$var_names)
  tm <- cbind(
    `vs BVAR`    = sapply(1:nn, function(i) nw_t(m$dfc[,4,i] - m$var[,4,i])),
    `vs DLM`     = sapply(1:nn, function(i) nw_t(m$dfc[,4,i] - m$dlm[,4,i])),
    `vs SV-BVAR` = sapply(1:nn, function(i) nw_t(m$dfc[,4,i] - m$svbvar[,4,i])))
  rownames(tm) <- m$var_names
  o <- order(tm[, 3])

  par(mar = c(4.2, 7.5, 2.4, 1))
  plot(NA, xlim = range(c(tm, -3, 5)), ylim = c(0.5, nn + 0.5), yaxt = "n",
       xlab = "Newey-West t   (positive = DGFC worse)", ylab = "",
       main = "All three comparisons", cex.main = 1, cex.lab = 0.9,
       cex.axis = 0.85)
  abline(h = 1:nn, col = "grey93")
  abline(v = c(-1.96, 1.96), lty = 2)
  abline(v = 0, col = "grey50")
  axis(2, at = 1:nn, labels = rownames(tm)[o], las = 1, cex.axis = 0.75, tick = FALSE)
  for (j in 1:3) points(tm[o, j], 1:nn, pch = 19, col = COL[j + 1], cex = 0.95)
  legend("bottomleft", colnames(tm), pch = 19, col = COL[2:4], bty = "o",
         cex = 0.8, horiz = FALSE, inset = c(0.06, 0.3))
}
```

The two comparisons already in the paper produce t-statistics up to 36, so the
test has ample power. The nulls against the SV BVAR are genuine, not a power
failure.

# Crime, Table 1 at saturated k

```{r crime-table, results = "asis"}
if (!has(F_CRIME)) {
  cat("`", F_CRIME, "` not found.\n\n", sep = "")
} else {
  ct    <- as.matrix(read.csv(F_CRIME))
  mods4 <- c("DGFC", "BVAR", "Pois-DGLM", "NB-DGLM")
  labL  <- c("Murder", "Attempted", "Accessory", "Manslaughter", "Non-domestic assault")
  labR  <- c("Officer assault", "Abduction", "Blackmail", "Escape custody", "Resist officer")

  crime_lab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:5, function(b) {
    rr <- (4 * b - 3):(4 * b)
    rbind(data.frame(series = labL[b], model = mods4, MAE = ct[rr, 1],
                     COV = ct[rr, 2], SIZE = ct[rr, 3], CRPS = ct[rr, 4],
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
          data.frame(series = labR[b], model = mods4, MAE = ct[rr, 5],
                     COV = ct[rr, 6], SIZE = ct[rr, 7], CRPS = ct[rr, 8],
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
  }))
  rownames(crime_lab) <- NULL
  write.csv(crime_lab, "crime_fcasts_k10_labeled.csv", row.names = FALSE)

  dgc <- crime_lab[crime_lab$model == "DGFC", ]
  nbc <- crime_lab[crime_lab$model == "NB-DGLM", ]
  srs <- dgc$series

  wins <- sapply(srs, function(s) {
    blk <- crime_lab[crime_lab$series == s, ]
    c(MAE = blk$MAE[1] == min(blk$MAE), SIZE = blk$SIZE[1] == min(blk$SIZE),
      CRPS = blk$CRPS[1] == min(blk$CRPS))
  })

  cat(sprintf("DGFC wins CRPS **%d of %d**, interval size **%d of %d**, and MAE **%d of %d**. Mean coverage %.3f against a 0.95 nominal. The NB-DGLM reaches %.3f but with intervals %.0f to %.0f times wider.\n\n",
              sum(wins["CRPS", ]), ncol(wins), sum(wins["SIZE", ]), ncol(wins),
              sum(wins["MAE", ]), ncol(wins), mean(dgc$COV), mean(nbc$COV),
              min(nbc$SIZE / dgc$SIZE), max(nbc$SIZE / dgc$SIZE)))

  wide <- data.frame(series = srs,
                     DGFC = dgc$CRPS,
                     BVAR = crime_lab$CRPS[crime_lab$model == "BVAR"],
                     Pois = crime_lab$CRPS[crime_lab$model == "Pois-DGLM"],
                     NB   = nbc$CRPS,
                     `cov DGFC`  = dgc$COV,
                     `size DGFC` = dgc$SIZE,
                     check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  # reorder to match the significance table below
  ord <- c("Murder", "Attempted", "Accessory", "Manslaughter", "Non-domestic assault",
           "Officer assault", "Abduction", "Blackmail", "Escape custody", "Resist officer")
  wide <- wide[match(ord, wide$series), ]
  rownames(wide) <- NULL

  print(knitr::kable(wide, caption = "Crime CRPS by model, with the DGFC's coverage and interval width. Full four-metric table in crime_fcasts_k10_labeled.csv."))
}
```

```{r crime-sig, results = "asis"}
F_CRIMESIG  <- "crime_k10_crps_per_origin.rds"
FORCE_CRIME <- FALSE   # TRUE to rebuild the cache even if it exists

cc <- NULL

if (!FORCE_CRIME && has(F_CRIMESIG)) {

  cc <- readRDS(F_CRIMESIG)

} else if (RUN_CRIME_SIG && has(F_CRIMEWS)) {

  # get_forecast_metrics() calls interval_score(), which exists in
  # scoringutils 1.2.2 and was removed in 2.x. Attached directly rather than
  # sourcing _packages.R, which tries to unload namespaces and fails once
  # bayesianVARs is loaded.
  suppressPackageStartupMessages({
    library(scoringutils); library(scoringRules); library(HDInterval)
  })
  if (!exists("interval_score"))
    stop("interval_score() not available. scoringutils is ",
         as.character(packageVersion("scoringutils")),
         "; this needs 1.2.2.")

  e <- new.env(); load(F_CRIMEWS, envir = e)
  if (!exists("get_variable_fcasts")) source("_helpers/_helpers.R")

  period <- (e$Tstart + e$H):e$Tstop    # defined after save.image, so rebuild
  ncr    <- ncol(e$Y)
  arrs   <- list(DGFC = e$fcast_dfc, BVAR = e$fcast_bvar,
                 `Pois-DGLM` = e$fcast_pois, `NB-DGLM` = e$fcast_nbinom)

  crps <- array(NA_real_, c(length(period), length(arrs), ncr),
                dimnames = list(NULL, names(arrs), e$my_labs))

  for (mn in names(arrs)) for (i in seq_len(ncr)) {
    s <- get_variable_fcasts(i, arrs[[mn]])
    crps[, mn, i] <- get_forecast_metrics(e$Y[period, i], s[period, , ],
                                          e$alpha)[1, "CRPS", 1, ]
  }

  cc <- list(crps = crps, labs = e$my_labs, period = period,
             source = F_CRIMEWS, built = Sys.time())
  saveRDS(cc, F_CRIMESIG)
  rm(e); gc()
}

if (!is.null(cc)) {

  ncr <- length(cc$labs)
  tt  <- function(a, b) sapply(seq_len(ncr),
                               function(i) nw_t(cc$crps[, a, i] - cc$crps[, b, i]))

  cs <- data.frame(series = cc$labs,
                   t_BVAR = round(tt("DGFC", "BVAR"), 2),
                   t_Pois = round(tt("DGFC", "Pois-DGLM"), 2),
                   t_NB   = round(tt("DGFC", "NB-DGLM"), 2),
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  print(knitr::kable(cs, caption = "Crime, Newey-West t on per-origin CRPS over 284 origins. Negative means the DGFC is better."))

  cat(sprintf("\n\nDGFC significantly better on %d of %d series against the BVAR, %d against the Poisson DGLM, and %d against the NB DGLM. Significantly worse on %d.\n\n",
              sum(cs$t_BVAR < -1.96), ncr, sum(cs$t_Pois < -1.96),
              sum(cs$t_NB < -1.96),
              sum(cs$t_BVAR > 1.96) + sum(cs$t_Pois > 1.96) + sum(cs$t_NB > 1.96)))

  cat(sprintf("_Per-origin CRPS cached in `%s`, built %s from `%s`._\n\n",
              F_CRIMESIG, format(cc$built, "%d %b %H:%M"), cc$source))
}

if (is.null(cc) && RUN_CRIME_SIG) {
  cat("Crime significance skipped: neither `", F_CRIMESIG, "` nor `",
      F_CRIMEWS, "` found.\n", sep = "")
}
```

# The ECDF ablation

Freezing the margin at the empirical CDF removes the uncertainty in F while
leaving everything else alone. This is the direct answer to what margin
estimation buys.

```{r ablation-text, results = "asis"}
# Built from macro_k14_metrics.rds rather than the CSV, so it can't drift
# out of sync with the rest of the document.
ab_m <- if (!is.null(m)) {
  f <- m$finals
  data.frame(series   = m$var_names,
             cov_ma   = f$dfc[, 2],  cov_ec = f$ecdf[, 2],
             size_pct = 100 * (f$ecdf[, 3] / f$dfc[, 3] - 1),
             crps_pct = 100 * (f$ecdf[, 4] / f$dfc[, 4] - 1),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
} else NULL
ab_c <- if (has(F_CRIMEA)) read.csv(F_CRIMEA, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) else NULL

if (!is.null(ab_c)) {
  cat(sprintf("**Crime.** Intervals narrow on %d of %d series and CRPS gets worse on %d, by up to %.0f%% on blackmail. Mean coverage falls %.3f to %.3f.\n\n",
              sum(ab_c$size_pct < 0), nrow(ab_c), sum(ab_c$crps_pct > 0),
              max(ab_c$crps_pct), mean(ab_c$cov_ma), mean(ab_c$cov_ec)))
}
if (!is.null(ab_m)) {
  lev <- ab_m$series %in% c("capu", "ur", "ffr", "spread")
  cat(sprintf("**Macro.** Intervals narrow on %d of %d and mean coverage falls %.3f to %.3f. CRPS improves on %d of the %d growth rates and breaks on capu, ur and ffr at %.0f%%, %.0f%% and %.0f%% worse.\n\n",
              sum(ab_m$size_pct < 0), nrow(ab_m),
              mean(ab_m$cov_ma), mean(ab_m$cov_ec),
              sum(ab_m$crps_pct[!lev] < 0), sum(!lev),
              ab_m$crps_pct[ab_m$series == "capu"],
              ab_m$crps_pct[ab_m$series == "ur"],
              ab_m$crps_pct[ab_m$series == "ffr"]))
}
```

```{r ablation-plot, fig.height = 4.4}
avail <- list(Crime = ab_c, Macro = ab_m)
avail <- avail[!sapply(avail, is.null)]

if (length(avail)) {
  par(mfrow = c(1, length(avail)), mar = c(7.5, 4, 2.6, 0.8))
  for (nm in names(avail)) {
    a <- avail[[nm]]
    barplot(rbind(a$cov_ma, a$cov_ec), beside = TRUE, las = 2,
            names.arg = a$series, ylim = c(0.70, 1.0), xpd = FALSE,
            border = NA, col = c(COL[1], "grey70"), cex.names = 0.55,
            cex.axis = 0.8, ylab = "empirical coverage", cex.lab = 0.85,
            main = paste(nm, "coverage"), cex.main = 1)
    abline(h = 0.95, lty = 2)
    if (nm == names(avail)[1])
      legend("topleft", c("margin adjustment", "ECDF"), fill = c(COL[1], "grey70"),
             border = NA, bty = "n", cex = 0.7, inset = c(0.4, -0.04))
  }
  par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
}
```

Freezing the margin costs calibration on both exercises. On crime it costs
accuracy as well.

# Where the macro loss sits

```{r era}
if (!is.null(m) && !is.null(m$gap)) {
  lev <- which(m$var_names %in% c("capu", "ur", "ffr", "spread"))
  scl <- colMeans(m$dfc[, 4, ])
  rel <- sweep(m$dfc[, 4, ] - m$svbvar[, 4, ], 2, scl, "/")

  eras <- data.frame(
    era = levels(m$era),
    all = round(as.numeric(tapply(rowMeans(rel), m$era, mean)), 4),
    levels_4 = round(as.numeric(tapply(rowMeans(rel[,  lev]), m$era, mean)), 4),
    growth_10 = round(as.numeric(tapply(rowMeans(rel[, -lev]), m$era, mean)), 4),
    vintages = as.numeric(table(m$era)), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  knitr::kable(eras, caption = "Relative CRPS advantage of the SV BVAR. Positive means the SV BVAR is ahead.")
}
```

```{r era-plot, fig.height = 3.8}
if (!is.null(m) && !is.null(m$gap)) {
  par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4.2, 4.2, 2.4, 0.8))

  plot(m$fdates, m$gap, type = "l", xlab = "forecast vintage",
       ylab = "rel. CRPS advantage, SV BVAR", main = "Per vintage",
       cex.main = 1, cex.lab = 0.85, cex.axis = 0.8)
  abline(h = 0, lty = 2); abline(v = c(2000, 2007, 2010), col = "grey85", lty = 3)

  mt <- rbind(as.numeric(tapply(rowMeans(rel[,  lev]), m$era, mean)),
              as.numeric(tapply(rowMeans(rel[, -lev]), m$era, mean)))
  barplot(mt, beside = TRUE, names.arg = levels(m$era), las = 2, border = NA,
          col = c(COL[4], "grey70"), ylab = "rel. CRPS advantage",
          main = "Levels vs growth", cex.main = 1, cex.names = 0.7,
          cex.axis = 0.8, cex.lab = 0.85)
  abline(h = 0)
  legend("topleft", c("4 levels", "10 growth"), fill = c(COL[4], "grey70"),
         border = NA, bty = "n", cex = 0.7)
  par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
}
```

The SV BVAR's advantage is **not** concentrated in the volatile period. It is
smallest in 2007 to 2009, the only era where the DGFC leads on growth rates,
and the largest single DGFC win in the sample is a 1991 vintage. The split is
by series, not by period.

# Mechanism

```{r mechanism, results = "asis"}
if (!is.null(d)) {
  mm <- round(colMeans(d$mech), 4)
  ee <- round(colMeans(d$eig), 4)

  cat(sprintf(
"The latent factor VAR sits at the stationarity boundary across the whole
posterior. The mean spectral radius of G is **%.4f** even among the
well-behaved draws, rising to **%.4f** in the worst 5%%, and the rejection
sampler is the only thing keeping it stationary.

The largest latent value is identical in both groups, %.4f against %.4f, so the
latent series is not compressed. What differs is the implied scale: %.4f
against %.4f, a ratio of %.2f. The stationary covariance of an AR(1) goes as
1/(1 - rho^2), which predicts a ratio of **%.2f** from those two spectral
radii.

Correlation between boundary proximity and the compressed margin: %.3f.
",
    ee["eig_good"], ee["eig_bad"], mm["maxz_bad"], mm["maxz_good"],
    mm["sdimp_bad"], mm["sdimp_good"], mm["sdimp_bad"] / mm["sdimp_good"],
    sqrt((1 - ee["eig_good"]^2) / (1 - ee["eig_bad"]^2)), ee["cor"]))
}
```

```{r mech-plot, fig.height = 3.8}
if (!is.null(d)) {
  par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4.2, 4.2, 2.4, 0.8))
  nvv <- nrow(d$eig)

  plot(d$vsel[seq_len(nvv)], d$eig[, "eig_good"], type = "b", pch = 19,
       ylim = c(min(d$eig[, c("eig_good", "eig_bad")]) - 0.004, 1.002),
       col = COL[1], xlab = "vintage index", ylab = "spectral radius of G",
       main = "Against the unit-root boundary", cex.main = 1, cex = 0.8,
       cex.lab = 0.85, cex.axis = 0.8)
  lines(d$vsel[seq_len(nvv)], d$eig[, "eig_bad"], type = "b", pch = 19,
        col = COL[2], cex = 0.8)
  abline(h = 1, lty = 2)
  legend("bottomright", c("typical draws", "worst 5%"), pch = 19,
         col = COL[1:2], bty = "n", cex = 0.7)

  barplot(as.numeric(d$tab$difference), names.arg = d$tab$dropped, border = NA,
          col = "grey70", xlab = "share of draws dropped",
          ylab = "CRPS penalty vs random (%)", cex.lab = 0.85, cex.axis = 0.8,
          cex.names = 0.8, main = "Dropping them makes it worse", cex.main = 1)
  abline(h = 0)
  par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
}
```

The draws nearest the boundary are not errors. Removing them degrades CRPS
monotonically against a random subsample of identical size, so they are
carrying real uncertainty about persistence.

```{r stable-note, results = "asis"}
if (!is.null(m) && !is.null(m$svbvar_nstable)) {
  cat(sprintf("The SV BVAR says the same thing from the other side. `stable = TRUE` discards non-stationary draws and keeps a median of %d of 5000, with %d of %d vintages keeping fewer than half.\n\n",
              round(median(m$svbvar_nstable)), sum(m$svbvar_nstable < 2500),
              length(m$svbvar_nstable)))
}
```

The macro data is not stationary, both models say so. The cost to the DGFC is
two series out of fourteen.

# Provenance

| Output | Produced by |
|:--------------------------------|:---------------------------------|
| `crime_fcasts_k10.csv`, `crime_ablation_k10.csv` | crime pipeline, k = 10, 5000/5000 |
| `macro_table_k14.csv`, `macro_ablation_k14.csv` | macro pipeline, k = 14, 5000/5000 |
| `macro_k14_metrics.rds` | macro pipeline post-processing |
| `degenerate_draw_test.rds` | `test_degenerate_draws.R`, 20 vintages |
| MCMC settings (5000 after 5000) | `dgfc_ess_diagnostic.R` |
| DGLM importance-weight degeneracy | `dglm_diagnostic.R` |
| Parallel refactor is faithful | `check_stage1.R` |
| ECDF flag is inert when off | `check_ecdf_flag.R` |

Checked and ruled out: time-varying volatility as the explanation for the SV
BVAR's edge; the spline's upper-tail extrapolation as a CRPS cost
(`test_pad_mult.R`, median change 0.0%); degenerate margin draws as a CRPS cost
(above).

Still open: the latent factor VAR is hardcoded to one lag while every macro
competitor uses four. Given that the binding constraint is persistence, that is
the remaining candidate, and it is a modelling decision rather than an
implementation one.
